drivers.variant_notes: Code update V6 (Spooky's DOM_v6.zip code update: DOM_V006.PRG, PRP_V008.BIN and the SD card's DMD/ and SFX/ folders), loaded as dominos_006.zip. Every edition (IPDB 6418 Standard Edition; IPDB 6586 Limited Edition) runs this code on the same board and playfield; PinMAME declares the set as a clone of the unreported pinHeck system set. PinMAME revisions before 97aa922b named it `dominos`.

physical.notes: Firmware cabinet input 1 (U12 D0), published at 1 by pinheck_brd_cab and SWITCH_UPDATE(pinheck). The Switch Edge walk toggled it separately (released, then held again) instead of closing it. The factory chart prints 'Coin Door (closed)' in this cell. pinheck_brd_reset sets it at every reset because the door rests closed; the ROM printed DOOR CLOSE while it was 1 and dropped the text when the host released it, so 1 means the door is closed. Cabinet header pin 'door', wire gray/white.

Firmware cabinet input 2 (U12 D1), published at 2 by pinheck_brd_cab and SWITCH_UPDATE(pinheck). The ROM's Switch Edge test drew this closure as firmware cabinet 2. PinMAME's port names the bit User; the factory chart leaves it blank and the cabinet header prints 'user0' without a wire colour.

Firmware cabinet input 3 (U12 D2), published at 3 by pinheck_brd_cab and SWITCH_UPDATE(pinheck). The Switch Edge walk drives the button through 112 instead, because core_updateSw rewrites this address every vblank. ROM-readable copy of the right flipper button: FLIP_SWNO(4, 3) makes core_updateSw copy public 112 into this address on every vblank, so a host drives 112; a direct write here is overwritten. Cabinet header pin 'R. flipper', wire gray/black.

Firmware cabinet input 4 (U12 D3), published at 4 by pinheck_brd_cab and SWITCH_UPDATE(pinheck). The Switch Edge walk drives the button through 114 instead, because core_updateSw rewrites this address every vblank. ROM-readable copy of the left flipper button: FLIP_SWNO(4, 3) makes core_updateSw copy public 114 into this address on every vblank, so a host drives 114; a direct write here is overwritten. Cabinet header pin 'L. flipper', wire gray/red.

Firmware cabinet input 5 (U12 D4), published at 5 by pinheck_brd_cab and SWITCH_UPDATE(pinheck). Not closed in the Switch Edge walk because it leaves the test; every walk used it to leave the test it ran. The factory switch chart leaves the cell blank but the wire chart's cabinet header wires 'menu' here; PinMAME's port names the bit Back, and the ROM leaves a test on it. Cabinet header pin 'menu', wire gray/blue.

Firmware cabinet input 6 (U12 D5), published at 6 by pinheck_brd_cab and SWITCH_UPDATE(pinheck). Not closed in the Switch Edge walk because it restarts the test; every walk opened the operator menu and started its test with it. Cabinet header pin 'enter', wire gray/green.

Firmware cabinet input 7 (U12 D6), published at 7 by pinheck_brd_cab and SWITCH_UPDATE(pinheck). The ROM's Switch Edge test drew this closure as firmware cabinet 7. Cabinet header pin 'coin mech', wire gray/purp.

Firmware cabinet input 8 (U12 D7), published at 8 by pinheck_brd_cab and SWITCH_UPDATE(pinheck). The ROM's Switch Edge test drew this closure as firmware cabinet 8. Cabinet header pin 'tilt', wire gray/yellow.

Factory switch 0, column 0, row 0. The ROM's Switch Edge test drew this closure at factory switch 0 (column 0, row 0) of its 8x8 grid. pinHeck reads the matrix uncomplemented: board.c pulls a return line low for every closed contact in the strobed column and the driver has no invSw mask, so public 1 is the closed contact. The ROM's Switch Edge test drew this closure while the host held public 1, so the contact rests open (normally_closed false), whatever its construction.

Firmware cabinet input 13 (U11 D5), published at 95 = 13 + 82. The ROM's Switch Edge test drew nothing for this closure. This is one of the two cabinet optos; the charts do not say which. The wire chart's OPTOS box names an Opto - 3 'Noid Loop' and an Opto - 4 'Scoop' pair (its captions sit over the other header's colours), the switch chart prints cabinet cells 13 and 14 as just 'Opto', the ROM's Switch Edge test does not name them, and PinMAME's simulator calls 95 the center ramp opto and 96 the oven ramp opto. pinHeck reads the matrix uncomplemented: board.c pulls a return line low for every closed contact in the strobed column and the driver has no invSw mask, so public 1 is the closed contact. The ROM's Switch Edge test drew this closure while the host held public 1, so the contact rests open (normally_closed false), whatever its construction.

mechanisms.behavior: Three balls rest on 12-14 (Trough Ball 1-3); the Ball Trough coil (18) feeds one to the shooter lane.
mechanisms.label: Three-ball trough

mechanisms.behavior: The Autolauncher (17) kicks the ball resting on the shooter lane switch 11 into play; PinMAME's simulator also offers a manual plunger here.
mechanisms.label: Shooter lane and autolauncher

mechanisms.behavior: A ROM-driven flipper on two board coils: the cabinet button reaches the ROM as cabinet input 3 (host public 112), the ROM fires the Right Flipper High (21) winding to lift the bat and holds it on the Right Flipper Low (19) winding, and the matrix end-of-stroke contact 15 tells it the stroke is complete. PinMAME publishes no Fliptronic states for this platform: the coil addresses are the flipper.
mechanisms.label: Right flipper

mechanisms.behavior: A ROM-driven flipper on two board coils: the cabinet button reaches the ROM as cabinet input 4 (host public 114), the ROM fires the Left Flipper High (10) winding to lift the bat and holds it on the Left Flipper Low (12) winding, and the matrix end-of-stroke contact 21 tells it the stroke is complete. PinMAME publishes no Fliptronic states for this platform: the coil addresses are the flipper.
mechanisms.label: Left flipper

mechanisms.behavior: Slingshot switch 22 closes and the ROM fires the Left Sling (11).
mechanisms.label: Left slingshot

mechanisms.behavior: Slingshot switch 16 closes and the ROM fires the Right Sling (20).
mechanisms.label: Right slingshot

mechanisms.behavior: The Left Scoop coil (9) ejects a ball held on 25.
mechanisms.label: Left scoop

mechanisms.behavior: The Right Scoop coil (13) ejects a ball held on 48.
mechanisms.label: Right scoop

mechanisms.behavior: The Up Post (7) between the orbits (36 right, 46 left) returns an orbit shot instead of letting it loop.
mechanisms.label: Orbit up-post

mechanisms.behavior: The Noid figure turns on servo 0 (57, the chart's Noid Orbit servo); 58 (Noid Home) closes when it is at home, and the Noid orbits 37/38 run past it. PinMAME's simulator models it as a continuous-rotation servo.
mechanisms.label: The Noid

mechanisms.behavior: Noid Bank Right/Middle/Left (26-28) on the target bank that servo 1 (58, Target Bank) lowers into the playfield.
mechanisms.label: Noid target bank
